clue.text: Town, it's plain, hiding new failure

indicators.note: a word hiding something holds it inside itself, so the plain wraps round the failure

parts.note: a llano is a grassy plain of South America
a dud is a flop or failure

explanation.surface: A remark that some town is plain and hides a new failure from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's plain' reads as a judgement of a dull town, but plain is the noun. LLANDUDNO is a seaside resort in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Llandudno is a resort in north Wales, an example of a town.

clue.text: A teacher is wrong

parts.note: pupils address a female schoolteacher as Miss

explanation.surface: A complaint that a schoolteacher has made a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is faulty or not right, a synonym of wrong.

clue.text: Very pale green at first, have you left grey at the end?

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word green

parts.note: thou hast is the old form of you have

indicators.note: at the end asks for only the closing letter of the word grey

explanation.surface: Someone asks a sickly friend whether they went from green to grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes G from green; 'at the end' takes Y from grey. HAST is the archaic second-person form of have.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghastly can describe a deathly white complexion, so it means extremely wan.

clue.text: Explosion setting army back: I drive off

indicators.note: setting the army back turns its letters round so they read the other way

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve
shoo is what you say to chase away a pest

explanation.surface: A military setback in which someone drives away after an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TA into AT. 'Explosion' is a sneeze here, and ATISHOO is the British spelling of the sound of a sneeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneeze is a sudden noisy expulsion of air, a little explosion from the nose.

clue.text: With no play area at first, game is in the balance

indicators.note: at first says the play-free area comes before the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: in rugby and football, touch is the area beyond the touchlines where the ball is out of play
and joins things in the way with does
Go is an oriental board game

explanation.surface: Without a play area to begin with, the outcome of a match is uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link but supplies AND; 'is' is the link. In rugby and football, touch is the ground beyond the touchline.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch and go describes an outcome that is risky and undecided, the idiom matching an uncertain state.

clue.text: Almost entirely give up

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: quite can mean completely or entirely

explanation.surface: An instruction to abandon something nearly completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the E from QUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to abandon or stop doing something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: What's in some gap that's found in alphabet

indicators.note: What's in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what fills some gap in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is an example of something found there.

clue.text: Incomplete box, say, among items chucked in current

indicators.note: among places the shortened tree inside the jettisoned items

parts.note: jetsam is cargo thrown overboard from a ship

indicators.note: incomplete says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: box is a kind of tree, so box, say is an example pointing to tree

explanation.surface: A broken box floats among the debris thrown into a current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box, say' reads as a container but is the box tree, an example of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet stream is a fast narrow air current high in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Fails to be accepted by priest, with name as Lothario

indicators.note: being accepted by something means being taken inside it

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
an engine dies when it fails

explanation.surface: A womaniser named by a priest fails to be welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'as' are links. Lothario became a byword through Rowe's eighteenth-century play.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario is the seducer in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent, so his name stands for a womaniser.

clue.text: Provide peer with one penny, not a pound

indicators.note: not a pound says those letters are to be left out of the word

parts.note: a peer is an equal, someone of the same standing
A plus L, the abbreviation for a pound (from Latin libra)
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A request to give a nobleman a penny instead of a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes A and L, the letters for 'a pound', so peer loses its last two letters before I and P join.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to furnish or supply someone with what they need.

clue.text: Starts to compile, and later finishes new jumbo?

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Advice to begin compiling and to finish the job later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' takes the first letters of compile, and, later, finishes. Jumbo is a common nickname for an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby elephant is called a calf, so a newborn jumbo is one.

clue.text: Act by ministry rejected in row, so no meaningful pattern here

indicators.note: in places the turned-round letters inside the word for a row

parts.note: a rank is a row of soldiers or taxis

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters for act and ministry read in reverse

parts.note: an act of parliament is a law
MOD is the Ministry of Defence

explanation.surface: A row breaks out after a ministry's act is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the act and ministry backwards (DOMWAL) before 'in' places them. MOD is the British Ministry of Defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A random walk is a mathematical path of successive random steps, so it shows no purposeful pattern.

clue.text: Book jazz singer to appear after autumn period

indicators.note: to appear after puts the singer behind the autumn month in the answer

parts.note: Nov is short for November, an autumn month
Ella Fitzgerald was the great American jazz singer

explanation.surface: A promoter books a jazz singer to perform after the autumn season.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, so it is a kind of book.

clue.text: Fat girl with an attitude going about

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it, so the attitude wraps the girl

parts.note: an becomes A and an attitude is a pose
Di is a short girl's name, from Diana

explanation.surface: A remark about a heavyweight girl with a bad attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat girl' tempts as a phrase, but Fat alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose means relating to or consisting of fatty tissue.

clue.text: Bird for one: about time

parts.note: for one introduces an example, abbreviated eg
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher says about time for one bird to show up.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Wonder if a rug can cover me during meditation

indicators.note: can cover says the rug lies around the other letters

parts.note: a mat is a small rug

indicators.note: during puts me inside the meditation word

parts.note: Zen is the Buddhist school of meditation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a yoga mat can be laid under them while meditating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if' is a link; 'can cover' and 'during' nest one container inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazement is a feeling of astonished awe, a synonym of wonder.

clue.text: Easy to carry guide in the dark

explanation.definitionFit: Light means not heavy, so easy to carry; a light is also a lamp that guides you through darkness.

clue.text: Mainly like beer, covering game

parts.note: as means like, in the same way

indicators.note: covering means the beer lies around the game

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A drinker's beer mostly ends up covering a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts the game inside the beer; the clue's lone 'a' sits between the pieces as written.
explanation.definitionFit: As a rule means usually or for the most part.

clue.text: Give up drink that's said to be dull

parts.note: to ditch something is to abandon or give it up
water is a drink

explanation.surface: A dieter gives up a drink that is reputed to be boring.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the saying 'as dull as ditchwater'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'dull as ditchwater' makes stagnant ditch water the proverbial byword for tedium.

clue.text: Senior teacher accepts you as old-fashioned

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the teacher holds the old word for you

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
ye is the archaic form of you

explanation.surface: A senior teacher welcomes someone as a traditionalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senior teacher' tempts as one phrase; Senior alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most senior or respected member of a group.

clue.text: Our cousin called, briefly out and about

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shortened words surround the telephoned word
briefly cuts the last letter off the phrase out and

parts.note: taken as written
rang means telephoned, that is called someone

explanation.surface: A relative telephoned briefly while out and about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims OUT AND to OUTAN, and 'about' puts RANG inside it. 'Our cousin' is apt: orang-utans are great apes, close relatives of humans.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape, a primate relative of humankind.

clue.text: A small number coming up the Central Line

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: six is a small number

explanation.surface: A commuter notes a small number of trains coming on the Central Line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns SIX into XIS. The Central Line is a London Underground line, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the central straight line about which something rotates or is symmetrical.

clue.text: One hopeless astride horse without outside help

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: astride means sitting with legs on either side, so the useless phrase straddles the horse

parts.note: no use means hopeless or futile
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A hopeless rider sits on a horse, refusing help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astride' puts H inside NO USE. 'horse' looks like a riding animal but is drug slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: In-house work is done within an organisation by its own staff rather than by outsiders.

clue.text: Peace increased, suppressing rise of imitative violent programme

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down inside, so peace and increased enclose the other letters

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet or peace
up means increased, as in prices going up

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: me-too describes a copycat or imitative product

explanation.surface: Peace has grown, suppressing the rise of copycat violent television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' turns ME TOO into OOTEM; 'Peace increased' looks like a phrase but is two pieces placed either side.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot-'em-up is a film or video game full of gunfire, a violent show.

clue.text: Get more efficient in the morning to crack Listener somehow

indicators.note: to crack means to break into, so the morning letters go inside
somehow says the letters of the word are arranged in some other way

parts.note: am is short for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A solver tries to crack the Listener crossword faster in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the letters (STRELINE). The Listener is a notoriously hard British crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: To streamline is to make a process simpler and more effective.

clue.text: So some prisoners released: just what pub needs

explanation.definitionFit: Paroled prisoners are freed on licence; a pub needs an on-licence permit to sell drinks for consumption on the premises.

clue.text: Post a bet on a Creole dish

parts.note: a jamb is the upright post of a door or window frame
to lay a bet is to place it, so lay means bet

explanation.surface: Someone places a bet on a spicy Creole dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Jambalaya is a Louisiana Creole rice dish with meat and seafood.

clue.text: Hand, one held by digger

indicators.note: held by means kept inside, so the digger holds the numeral

parts.note: a delver is one who digs
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A labourer holds a single hand tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts I inside DELVER. 'Hand' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand something over is to pass or give it, a synonym.

clue.text: Generally agreed a French bird has lost tail

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: losing its tail means the bird word drops its last letter

parts.note: the avocet is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A French bird has lost its tail, all agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost tail' cuts AVOCET to AVOCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Una voce is Latin for with one voice, meaning unanimously.

clue.text: Goddess offers a help up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an is a form of the article a
aid means help

explanation.surface: A goddess offers someone a helping hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AN AID into DIANA; 'offers' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt.

clue.text: Got down time after short sound of bell

indicators.note: after puts the time letter behind the shortened bell sound
short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a knell is the tolling of a bell

explanation.surface: A congregation kneels in time after the bell has briefly tolled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims KNELL to KNEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To have knelt is to have gone down on one's knees.

clue.text: Stomach accommodates large excess

indicators.note: accommodates means takes in, so the stomach holds the large letter

parts.note: gut means stomach
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: A big stomach makes room for a large surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodates' puts L inside GUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A glut is an oversupply, a surplus.
